chunk_findings.detail: `isolate_venv` only creates a `.venv` directory; it does not make later uv/pip commands use that directory. If the ddflow/agent process has `VIRTUAL_ENV` pointing at the primary shared `.venv` (common when the primary venv is activated) or has the primary `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`, uv/pip select the shared environment regardless of the newly created worktree-local `.venv`. For example: activate `/repo/.venv`, run `ddflow create` for a worktree, then run `uv pip install -e .` inside that worktree. uv honors `VIRTUAL_ENV=/repo/.venv` and rewrites `/repo/.venv/.../_editable_impl_ddflow_mcp.pth` to point at the worktree, so removing the worktree again leaves ddflow console scripts broken. The new guard returns `True` and clean-environment tests pass, but the original failure mode persists in this environment.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:isolate_venv

chunk_findings.detail: The early return `if (venv / "pyvenv.cfg").is_file(): return False` follows symlinks, so a worktree `.venv` that is merely a symlink to the primary `.venv` is treated as already isolated. Given `ln -s /repo/.venv /repo/.ddflow/worktrees/bug/.venv`, `isolate_venv` returns without creating a worktree-local environment; a later `uv pip install -e .` run in the worktree resolves the symlinked `.venv` to the shared primary venv and repoints its editable install. The guard should reject symlinked or non-local `.venv` targets before deciding the worktree is isolated.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:isolate_venv

chunk_findings.detail: The symlink cleanup is performed before the function checks whether `uv` is available and before it knows that `uv venv` can succeed. Given a worktree with `uv.lock`, a `.venv` symlink to a valid non-shared local environment, and `uv` absent from `PATH` (or `uv venv` failing, e.g. disk full), `isolate_venv` executes `venv.unlink()` and then returns `False`, destroying the existing local `.venv` marker without replacing it. A later `uv pip install -e .` after `uv` becomes available can find no worktree-local `.venv` and walk up to the shared primary `.venv`, reproducing the editable-install repoint. The cleanup should be deferred until `uv` is known to be usable, and ideally until the replacement venv can actually be created.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:isolate_venv

chunk_findings.detail: `venv.unlink(missing_ok=True)` suppresses only `FileNotFoundError`. If the worktree `.venv` is a symlink that cannot be removed because the parent directory is read-only/immutable or the symlink is otherwise protected, the call raises `PermissionError`/`OSError` instead of returning `False`. This contradicts the function’s documented “never raised” / “a failure to make the venv is skipped” contract and the existing pattern of using `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` for non-rebuildable leftovers; claim creation can die on such a filesystem state.

This contradicts the function’s documented “never raised” / “a failure to make the venv is skipped” contract and the existing pattern of using `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` for non-rebuildable leftovers; claim creation can die on such a filesystem state.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:isolate_venv

chunk_findings.detail: The destructive cleanup is still performed before the function knows that `uv venv` can succeed. Moving `shutil.which("uv")` above the cleanup only handles the case where the `uv` binary is absent; it does not handle the case where `uv` exists but `uv venv` fails. For example, if a worktree has `.venv` symlinked to a valid non-shared local environment and `uv` is on `PATH` but exits non-zero (e.g. a fake `uv` script, disk full, quota exceeded, or timeout), `isolate_venv` unlinks the symlink before invoking `uv venv`, then the command fails. The previous worktree-local `.venv` marker has been destroyed even though no replacement was created. The prior confirmed finding explicitly included “uv venv failing”; this delta only checks `which uv`, so that part of the defect remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:isolate_venv

data.probe: Confirmed: cleanup still ran before knowing uv venv would succeed; an existing symlink was destroyed when uv venv then failed. Fixed in c546f5ee2: isolate_venv now builds the venv into a sibling .tmp path and only swaps it in after uv venv succeeds and writes pyvenv.cfg; a failing uv venv returns False leaving the existing .venv untouched.
data.title: ddflow/infra/worktree/_create.py:isolate_venv

chunk_findings.detail: The patch replaces `shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)` with `fsio.rmtree(tmp)` and removes `import shutil`, but it does not add `from .. import fsio` in this file (the file’s manifest delta is `+1/-2`, while the sibling worktree files that needed the import are `+2/-2`). When the scratch cleanup path runs after `claimed.unlink()`, the name `fsio` is not defined, so the code raises `NameError: name 'fsio' is not defined` instead of removing `tmp` and running `git worktree prune`.

chunk_findings.detail: The change raises the allowed agent-literal count for `ddflow/config_sections/agent.py` from 6 to 7 instead of fixing the newly admitted `grok` literal in code. With this baseline, a source edit that introduces `grok` into that module passes the guard even though the guard’s purpose is to prevent such literals; this directly contradicts the stated intent that moved sites be re-keyed with counts unchanged and that the fix be made “by code, not baseline raising.” The baseline increase weakens the guard and hides the new literal.

chunk_findings.detail: The new allowlist writes the revoked Gemini key as a literal into `.gitleaks.toml`, but the allowlist is scoped with `condition = "AND"` and a path regex that only matches `.ddflow/events/...`. When gitleaks scans the repository or staged changes, it scans `.gitleaks.toml` itself; the literal key in the `regexes` value matches the `gcp-api-key` detector, while the path condition does not match `.gitleaks.toml`, so this new occurrence is not allowlisted. Thus the change introduces a scanner hit in the config file itself and can fail CI/`gitleaks protect` even though it suppresses the original event-log occurrence.
chunk_findings.title: .gitleaks.toml `regexes = ['''[REDACTED]''']`

chunk_findings.detail: The sequential-filler allowlist is an unanchored global regex, so it suppresses any detected secret that merely contains `1234567890Abcdefghij`, not only the standalone example quoted in the event log. For example, a real credential such as `[REDACTED]` in any file would be allowlisted by this regex, contradicting the comment that the value is “named per value” and that a real key still fires. The same issue applies to the `[REDACTED]` allowlist.
chunk_findings.title: .gitleaks.toml `regexes = ['''1234567890Abcdefghij''']`

chunk_findings.detail: The change modifies gitleaks allowlist behavior but includes no regression test. The stated workflow requires a test that fails on the unfixed code, but the manifest contains only `.gitleaks.toml`; there is no test fixture asserting that the known event-log shard is ignored while a live `AIza` key outside that path still fires, nor that the config’s own literal does not create a new finding. Without such a test, over- or under-suppression regressions can be introduced silently, as shown by the self-detection and unanchored-regex issues above.
chunk_findings.title: .gitleaks.toml change as a whole

chunk_findings.detail: The diff adds the revoked Gemini key as a literal regex value in `.gitleaks.toml`, so after this commit the tracked config file itself contains a second occurrence of the key: `git grep [REDACTED]` will match both the event-log shard and `.gitleaks.toml`. The earlier probe only shows that the current `gitleaks git` invocation does not report a finding from its own config; it does not remove the literal from the repository. Any secret scanner that does not exempt config files (GitHub secret scanning, trufflehog, or a future gitleaks configuration that stops skipping `.gitleaks.toml`) will see a new copy outside the event-log path allowlist. Given the stated bug is that the leaked key is still present on main/origin, this change does not fix that condition and adds another tracked copy.
